title: Deep Convolutional Networks for Skin Lesion Classification
problem: Classifying dermoscopic images of skin lesions into benign and malignant categories.
method: A CNN-based pipeline trained end-to-end on dermoscopic images.
evaluation: Accuracy, sensitivity, and AUC on a held-out test split.
results: The proposed CNN achieved 91.2% accuracy and 0.94 AUC, outperforming a Random Forest baseline built on handcrafted texture features.
limitation: Performance drops noticeably on darker Fitzpatrick skin tones due to dataset imbalance, an open problem for future work.

title: Hybrid Texture-and-Deep-Feature Fusion for Melanoma Detection
problem: Detecting melanoma from dermoscopic images under limited labeled data.
method: Combines Gabor filters, Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) with a Random Forest classifier, benchmarked against a deep CNN baseline.
results: The hand-crafted feature fusion reached F1 of 0.83, close to the CNN baseline's 0.86, while training in a fraction of the time.
limitation: Hand-crafted features remain competitive on small data but do not generalize across imaging devices from different manufacturers.

title: Vision Transformers for Chest X-ray Disease Classification
problem: Multi-label classification of 14 thoracic diseases from chest radiographs.
method: A Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture using patch embedding and self-attention, pretrained on ImageNet then fine-tuned.
results: The ViT model achieved a mean AUROC of 0.812 across 14 classes, modestly beating a ResNet-50 baseline at 0.795.
limitation: Interpretability of attention maps for radiologist trust remains unresolved; clinicians in a pilot study found the maps difficult to act on.

title: Federated Learning for Mammography Screening Across Hospitals
problem: Training breast cancer detection models across multiple hospital sites without sharing raw mammography images.
method: A federated learning framework using FedAvg combined with differential privacy noise injection.
dataset: Multi-site private mammograms plus CBIS-DDSM for external validation.
evaluation: Sensitivity and specificity at a fixed false-positive rate.
results: The federated model reached 88% sensitivity at a fixed 10% false-positive rate, within 2 points of a centrally-trained model.
limitation: Communication overhead scales poorly beyond 10 participating sites, limiting real-world hospital network deployment.

title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
problem: Grading diabetic retinopathy severity from retinal fundus images with limited labeled data.
method: Contrastive self-supervised pretraining (SimCLR-style) followed by supervised fine-tuning for 5-class grading.
evaluation: Quadratic weighted kappa against ophthalmologist grading.
results: Self-supervised pretraining improved quadratic weighted kappa from 0.71 (supervised-only) to 0.79.
limitation: Cross-population generalization across different camera vendors is not evaluated in this study.

title: Explainable AI for Histopathology Cancer Grading
problem: Grading prostate cancer aggressiveness (Gleason grading) from histopathology whole-slide images.
method: A CNN model with Grad-CAM and attention-based explainability overlays.
evaluation: Quadratic kappa and a pathologist agreement study.
results: Model-pathologist agreement reached a quadratic kappa of 0.74, comparable to inter-pathologist agreement in the literature.
limitation: Explanations are not validated against ground-truth cellular annotations, raising questions about explanation faithfulness.

title: Multi-Modal Fusion of MRI and Genomic Data for Brain Tumor Subtyping
problem: Classifying glioma molecular subtypes to guide treatment planning.
method: Fusion of 3D CNN features extracted from MRI scans with genomic expression data via a joint embedding layer.
dataset: TCGA-GBM/LGG genomic cohort combined with the BraTS MRI dataset.
evaluation: Balanced accuracy and survival correlation analysis.
results: The fused model achieved 84% balanced accuracy versus 76% for an MRI-only baseline.
limitation: Small genomic cohort size limits statistical power for rare molecular subtypes.

title: Synthetic Data Augmentation via GANs for Rare Skin Disease Classification
problem: Addressing severe class imbalance for rare dermatological conditions.
method: A conditional GAN generates synthetic dermoscopic images of rare conditions to augment training data.
dataset: Augmented ISIC dataset plus a private rare-disease image set.
evaluation: Downstream classifier accuracy improvement with vs without synthetic augmentation.
results: Synthetic augmentation improved minority-class recall by 12 percentage points.
limitation: Synthetic image realism was judged only qualitatively, not validated by dermatologists.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Deep Learning for Radiology Triage
problem: Flagging low-confidence chest CT predictions for radiologist review in a triage setting.
method: Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles used to estimate predictive uncertainty.
evaluation: Calibration error and triage efficiency (cases correctly deferred to human review).
results: Uncertainty-based triage reduced radiologist workload by 22% while deferring 95% of true errors for manual review.
limitation: No prospective clinical trial has evaluated the real-world workflow impact of this triage approach.

title: Cross-Institution Generalization of Deep Learning Skin Cancer Classifiers
problem: Understanding why skin cancer classifiers trained at one institution fail to generalize elsewhere.
method: A ResNet-50 baseline benchmarked across institutions, plus domain adaptation experiments.
evaluation: AUC drop when testing across different collection sites.
results: AUC dropped from 0.93 in-domain to 0.79 on an external site, even after standard domain adaptation.
limitation: The generalization gap remains largely unresolved; explicitly called out as an open problem in dermatology AI.

title: Lightweight Mobile CNNs for Point-of-Care Skin Lesion Screening
problem: Enabling on-device skin lesion triage in low-resource settings with limited compute.
method: A MobileNetV3-based architecture optimized for latency and model size.
dataset: A subset of the ISIC dataset.
evaluation: Accuracy versus inference-time trade-off on mobile hardware.
results: The model achieved 87% accuracy at 45ms inference time on a mid-range smartphone CPU.
limitation: Not validated on smartphone camera images captured under real field conditions.

title: Attention-Based Multi-Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification
problem: Classifying gigapixel histopathology slides without requiring patch-level labels.
method: A multi-instance learning framework with attention-based pooling over slide patches.
results: The attention-MIL model achieved 0.91 AUC, with attention maps loosely correlated to tumor regions.
limitation: Attention weights correlate imperfectly with tumor regions as confirmed by pathologist review.

title: Ensemble of CNN Architectures for COVID-19 Detection from CT Scans
problem: Detecting COVID-19 from chest CT scans during the early pandemic period.
method: An ensemble combining ResNet, DenseNet, and EfficientNet backbones.
results: The ensemble reached 0.96 AUC on the original test set.
limitation: The dataset was collected early in the pandemic and may not reflect later viral variants or updated scanner protocols.

title: Contrastive Domain Adaptation for Retinal Image Quality Assessment
problem: Assessing retinal fundus image quality automatically across different camera manufacturers.
method: A contrastive domain adaptation method trained to be invariant to camera-specific artifacts.
evaluation: Quality classification accuracy measured across camera domains.
results: Cross-domain quality classification accuracy improved from 74% to 89% after domain adaptation.
limitation: Quality assessment does not yet feed back into downstream diagnostic accuracy measurement.

title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning vs Deep Learning for Tabular Clinical Risk Prediction
problem: Predicting 30-day hospital readmission risk from structured EHR data (not imaging).
method: Gradient boosted trees compared against a deep tabular model (TabNet).
results: Gradient boosted trees slightly outperformed TabNet, 0.81 vs 0.79 AUROC.
limitation: Included here as a plausible but off-target match for an imaging-focused review; tests topic filtering.

title: Large Language Models for Clinical Note Summarization
problem: Summarizing free-text clinical notes into structured discharge summaries.
method: Fine-tuning a large language model on note-summary pairs.
results: Physician reviewers rated 82% of generated summaries as clinically acceptable without edits.
limitation: This is an NLP-for-healthcare paper, not diagnostic imaging; included to test topic filtering against near-domain distractors.

title: Predictive Maintenance for Hospital MRI Machine Uptime Using Sensor Data
problem: Predicting maintenance needs for MRI scanner hardware to reduce downtime.
method: Time-series anomaly detection applied to sensor logs from MRI machines.
evaluation: Precision and recall of failure prediction.
results: The anomaly detector predicted 78% of failures at least 48 hours in advance.
limitation: Mentions 'MRI' but concerns equipment reliability, not diagnostic image analysis - a keyword-collision distractor for topic filtering.
